chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The sick person who is overcome, and the one who has fainted, the stoning is done on his behalf and he is carried around for tawaf.

key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبُ: the one overcome by weakness or incapacity
key_terms.الْمُغْمَىٰ عَلَيْهِ: the one who has fainted or is unconscious
key_terms.يُرْمَىٰ: the rite of stoning is performed
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: he is taken around for tawaf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for tawaf and ramy for a sick or unconscious pilgrim?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pilgrim who is incapacitated by illness or unconsciousness. It states that the rite of ramy is performed on his behalf, while tawaf is performed with him being carried.
